text:
alex.m: heads up — we've got a spike in ephemeral NVMe IOPS in ap-southeast1 that's blocking GPU provisioning, seen ~80% attach failures in the last 10m
toni: ugh, is this the janitor scrub kicking off?
kevin: yes, looks correlated with nightly scrub ramp + a customer batch job that started earlier, both hitting the same hosts
maria: logs?
alex.m: paste of the attach error logs: ```
ERR attach: failed to mount scratch: i/o timeout, NVMe QDepth=128, write_wait=34ms
WARN nvme: async queue full, backlog 256
```
toni: that async queue full line is the giveaway — scrub concurrency needs to be lower or we'll keep stalling attaches
kevin: we can throttle scrub in ap-southeast1 to 2 concurrent workers and pause the deep-scan cohort for 30m as a mitigation
alex.m: can we do that without causing wear backlog regression? cost tradeoff?
maria: short pause should be fine, backlog will grow but not catastrophic for 30-60m. Cost of failed GPU attaches >> delayed scrub.
ops-bot: deploy started by kevin: scrub-throttle-ap-southeast1 -> in-progress
toni: also let's pin affected allocation to fallback pool with higher IOPS for the next 20min so in-flight jobs can attach
kevin: doing that now. routing the provisioning requests to hi-iops pool in ap-southeast1 via policy override
alex.m: quick patch applied: scrub concurrency -> 2 (was 8). Janitor cohort deep-scan delayed by 45m. Monitoring dashboards updated.
maria: watch for wear amplification — lower concurrency reduces instantaneous IOPS but extends time scrub runs; flag if scrub backlog > 12h
toni: noted. can we add a temporary guard in provisioning to prefer dedicated / reserved nodes for big batch jobs? that would avoid hopscotch into scrub-heavy machines
kevin: product already has reserved tag but not enforced. I'll open a follow-up ticket to respect reserved tags for >X GPU attach requests.
alex.m: can we get a heatmap of IOPS per-host over the last hour? need to see if any single host is the root cause
maria: grabbing that now. initial look: 6 hosts at 10-12k iops, rest under 2k. Looks like scrub + one heavy batch job hitting a handful of nodes (hotstripe).
toni: maybe we should add a locality-aware scrub scheduler so scrubs avoid nodes currently serving GPU attach windows
kevin: agree. longer term: add attach-safe windows and integrate with GPU scheduler. short term: I've bumped hi-iops pool capacity by 12 GPUs to absorb the attach failures
ops-bot: alert resolved: attach-error-rate in ap-southeast1 -> back to baseline
alex.m: attach errors dropped after throttle and pool bump. keeping this thread open for next 2 hours to watch for regressions. :thumbsup:
